title: The clock on your phone is not the clock that leaves.
subtitle: Ship's time, all-aboard, and the last tender are three different numbers.

sub: It is printed in the daily programme and posted at the gangway, and it is stated in ship's time. Sailing time is not your deadline — all-aboard is.

title: Three clocks on a port day

items.head: Ship's time
items.body: The only one that matters. On a repositioning sailing it advances an hour a day and stops agreeing with shore.

items.head: Local time
items.body: Whatever your phone picks up from the nearest mast. Useful for a lunch reservation and nothing else.

items.head: The last tender
items.body: Where the ship anchors instead of docking, this is a separate and earlier time. Read both, every time.

title: Two travellers in the same taverna

right.label: On ship time
items: An hour spare in the old town

text: Departure slots belong to the port, not to the bridge.
sub: Berth scheduling and maritime requirements set the hour. This was Disney's stated position after Dublin, and it is the honest one — holding the ship is often simply not available.

quote: Set your watch to ship's time at breakfast on day one, and then never look at your phone for a departure again.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: They are the one reading a phone clock at ten to five. Tell me the sailing you're weighing and I'll send back a two-line verdict on its port days.
